Chhattisgarh raises honorarium for tribal representatives ahead of Diwali, officials say

Background to Muria Darbar and Bastar Dussehra

The annual Bastar Dussehra, a 75‑day celebration of tribal culture in Chhattisgarh, culminates in the Muria Darbar ceremony in Bastar district. The event brings together traditional tribal representatives, known locally as mān̐jhīs (tribal council members) and chālakīs (female drivers who assist in ceremonial processions). This year, the ceremony was attended by President Droupadi Murmu, marking the first time a sitting President has participated in the ritual.

Details of the honorarium increase

During the Muria Darbar, the state government announced a revision of the monthly honorarium paid to these representatives:

  • Mān̐jhīs: from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000 per month.
  • Chālakīs: from ₹1,500 to ₹3,500 per month.

The announcement was made in the presence of President Murmu and was described by officials as a “gift” before the Diwali festival.

Government rationale and statements

State Minister Rajesh Agrawal said the increase reflects the administration’s commitment to honoring traditional representatives and promoting their economic empowerment. He attributed the decision to Chief Minister Vishnu Dev Sai and framed it as part of a broader effort to preserve Bastar’s cultural heritage while supporting tribal livelihoods.

Chief Minister Vishnu Dev Sai, speaking at the event, highlighted the symbolic importance of the Muria Darbar as a “beautiful expression of tribal culture and democratic tradition.” He linked the honorarium revision to the state’s ongoing development agenda for Bastar, noting that the region is moving away from past Maoist‑related violence toward new growth initiatives.

Wider development context in Bastar

The honorarium announcement was accompanied by references to several infrastructure and social‑welfare projects underway in the district:

  • Transportation: A new rail service from Raipur to Ravghat has begun, with work continuing on the Ravghat‑Jagdalpur line. The Raipur‑Visakhapatnam expressway now passes through Bastar, improving road connectivity.
  • Rural schemes: Implementation of the Niyad Nellanara plan, the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, and the PM‑Jan Dhan scheme aims to extend government benefits to remote villages.
  • Tourism and hospitality: Special provisions for homestays are being introduced to promote cultural tourism.
  • Health and education: A super‑speciality hospital in Jagdalpur and a new medical college in Gidam have started operations. Plans for an “Education City” in Orcha and Jagargunda are also in progress.

These initiatives were presented as part of a “road‑map” for Bastar’s socioeconomic development, with the government citing events such as Bastar Pandum and Bastar Olympics as catalysts for cultural promotion and economic activity.

Practical implications for Mān̐jhīs and Chālakīs

The revised honorarium translates to a 150 % increase for mān̐jhīs and a 133 % increase for chālakīs. Assuming a full‑time engagement, the monthly boost could improve household income, enable better access to education and health services, and reduce reliance on informal labor. However, the announcement did not specify whether the increase will be retroactive, how it will be funded, or the exact mechanism for disbursement.

What remains uncertain / verification

  • Funding source: The state’s budget allocation for the higher honorarium was not disclosed.
  • Implementation timeline: No date was given for when the new rates will take effect.
  • Eligibility criteria: It is unclear whether all existing mān̐jhīs and chālakīs will receive the increase or only those officially recognized by the Muria Darbar committee.

Readers can verify the announcement by consulting the original report published by *Navbharat Times* on the Chhattisgarh government’s website: https://navbharattimes.indiatimes.com/state/chhattisgarh/raipur/major-gift-from-government-ahead-of-diwali-honorarium-for-manjhis-and-chalakis/articleshow/135150528.cms The article includes statements from Minister Rajesh Agrawal and details of the ceremony attended by President Droupadi Murmu.

--- *This article is based solely on the information released by the Chhattisgarh government and reported by *Navbharat Times*. No independent interviews were conducted.*
